chat.author: Jeffrey Haas
chat.text:
I won't fight for mic time, but a common issue we've run into is RFCs containing conflicting or use-case-specific modifications of a given term. But part of that for BGP is simply its age and inconsistency of editors across decades.
Some place that has the expected common definition is helpful, even if it gets used as part of I-D boilerplate for the section.  The wiki is one such place it can be kept - github another - a zombie I-D a third.

chat.author: John Scudder

chat.text: I appreciate the eff out of it when someone reviews one of my documents.

chat.author: Joel Jaeggli
chat.text:
yeah in general I think the observation about unsolicited reviews is overstated.  
not all review comments or aesthetic preferences are blocking anyway

chat.author: Joel Jaeggli
chat.text: some are simply opinions and do not reflect a lack of consent with the working groups choices.

chat.author: Joel Jaeggli
chat.text: extra work comes at a cost though

chat.author: John Scudder
chat.text: Agreed. In my case when I was an AD I tried to make sure all review comments had been addressed. But, "addressed" could mean "your comment has been heard. I'm not going to do that, though."

chat.author: Geoff Huston
chat.text: I'm relating my experience in the DNS directorate - we work in a mode of chair and ad-assigned review tasks and the expectation is that review comments are addressed in a dialogue begtween the reviewer and the authors.
